textbookText: 22. A ball with a mass of 0.1 kg is thrown vertically upwards with a velocity of 20 ms-1. What is the potential energy at the maximum height? What is the potential energy of the ball when it reaches three-quarters of the maximum height while moving upwards? (Ans: 20J, 15J)

23. A block with a mass of 20 kg slides down the surface of a bowl with a diameter of 0.5 meters, moving from the top to the bottom. Calculate the speed of the ball as it reaches the bottom. ( Ans:2.24 ms-1)

24. An object moves along a certain path from point A with position vector r⃗1=3î+2ĵ to point B with position vector r⃗2=2î +3ĵ under the force F⃗⃗=î+ĵ. Find out the work done by the force. (Ans: 0 J)
25. A particle moves along the x-axis from x=0 to x=5 m under the influence of a force given by F=3x2-2x+7. Find the work done in this force. (Ans:135J)

26. A car of mass 1000 kg moves at a constant speed of 20 ms-1 along a horizontal road where the frictional force is 200N. Calculate the power developed by the engine. If the car, now, moves up an incline at the same constant speed, calculate the new power developed by the engine. Assume that the frictional force is still 200N and that sin θ= 1 , where θ is the angle of the inclination to the horizontal. (Ans: 4 kW,14Kw)

27. While playing a football match, player A collided and got entangled with player B who was playing for the opposite team and running from the opposite side. The mass of player A was 40 kg and the mass of player B was 60 kg. If player B was running with a velocity of 3ms-1 and player B was running with a velocity of 4 ms-1, find the velocity and direction of both players after collision assuming other forces were negligible. ( Ans: -0.2 ms-1)
28. A train of mass 2.0 x105 kg moves at a constant speed of 72 km h-1 up a straight incline against a frictional force of 1.28 × 104 N. The incline is such that the train
rises vertically 1.0 m for every 100 m traveled along the incline. Calculate (i) the rate of increase per second of the train and (ii) the necessary power developed by the train.
(Ans:(i)400kW (ii)656kW)
29. A stationary radioactive nucleus of mass 210 units disintegrates into an alpha particle of mass 4 units and a residual nucleus of mass 206 units. If the kinetic energy of the
alpha particle is E, calculate the kinetic energy of the residual nucleus. (Ans: 2 𝐸)
30. A railway truck of mass 4 x 104 kg moving a velocity of 3 ms-1 collides with another
truck of mass 2 × 104 kg which is at rest. The coupling joins and the trucks move off
together. What fraction of the first truck’s initial kinetic energy remains as kinetic
energy of two trucks after the collision?
(Ans: 2 )
31. A bullet of mass 0.010 kg is fired vertically with a velocity of 100 ms-1 into a wooden
block of mass 0.190 kg suspended by a long string above the gun. If the bullet is embedded in the block, through what height does the block move? (Ans: 1.25 m)

32. A vehicle of mass 2000 kg travelling at 10ms-1 on a horizontal surface is brought to rest at a distance of 12.5 m by the action of its brakes. Calculate the average retarding force. What power must the engine develop in order to take the vehicle up an incline of 1 in 10 at a constant speed of 10 ms-1, if the frictional resistance is equal to200N? (Ans:8000N,22kW)

33. You push your physics book 1.50 m along a horizontal tabletop with a horizontal force of 2.40 N. The opposing force of friction is 0.600 N. (a) How much work does your 2.40 N force do on the book? (b) What is the work done on the book by the friction force? (c) What is the total work done on the book? (Ans: (a)3.6J,(b)0.9J,(c)2.7J)
34. How many joules of energy does a 100-watt light bulb use per hour? How fast would a 70 kg person have to run to have that amount of energy? (Ans:3.6 × 105J,100ms-1 )

35. A ball with a mass 0.420 kg is initially moving with a speed of 2.00 ms-1. A player kicks the ball, exerting a constant force of magnitude 40.0N in the same direction as the ball’s motion. Over what distance must her foot be in contact with the ball to increase the ball’s speed to 6.00 ms-1? (Ans:0.168 m)

36. A worker applies a constant horizontal force of 80N to a block of ice on a smooth horizontal floor. The frictional force is negligible. The block starts from rest and moves 11 m in 5 s. (i) What is the mass of the block of ice? (ii) If the worker stops pushing at the end of 5 s, how far does the block move in the next 5 s? (Ans:90.9 kg,22m)

37. A 6.0 kg box moving at 3.0 ms-1 on a horizontal, frictionless surface runs into a light spring of force constant 75 N/cm. Use the work-energy theorem to find the maximum compression of the spring. (Ans:0.085m)

38. A tandem (two-person) bicycle team must overcome a force of 165N to maintain a speed of 9.00 ms-1. Find the power required per rider, assuming that each contributes equally. Express your answer in watts and in horsepower. (Ans:742.5 watt) Arrange questions as per the units unless they are integrated.
